answers.answer: No. SCOPe 2.08 does not treat them as one homologous superfamily. They are three separate superfamilies under one shared fold, f.21 "Heme-binding four-helical bundle" (class f, membrane and cell surface proteins). The superfamilies are f.21.1 Transmembrane di-heme cytochromes (sunid 81342), f.21.2 Fumarate reductase respiratory complex transmembrane subunits (sunid 81343), and f.21.3 Respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain (sunid 103501). In SCOPe the fold level records a shared architecture and topology. It does not claim common ancestry. Superfamily is the level at which SCOPe groups domains it judges to be evolutionarily related, from structural and functional evidence such as conserved heme-ligand features, even when sequence similarity is low. Because the three groups sit in different superfamilies, SCOPe does not assert that they are homologous. Their similar heme-binding four-helix bundles could come from convergence or from a relationship too distant to document, and SCOPe leaves that open. Do not infer shared function, mechanism, heme-ligation geometry, or a usable modelling template from fold membership. A fold-level link supports only a topological comparison. Calling them one superfamily would need extra evidence, such as significant sequence or profile links, conserved heme-ligating residues, or a revised SCOPe classification. Within each superfamily, homology is the supported claim, and the family level indicates closer relationships.
